question: A 56-year-old woman undergoes open reduction and internal fixation of the distal tibia 1 day after a fall. She has had rheumatoid arthritis for 12 years and diabetes mellitus for 2 years. Her medications over the past year have included metformin, prednisone, calcium supplements, and methotrexate. Prior to surgery, insulin was added to her medications, and the dose of prednisone was increased. She has had appropriate nutrition over the years with regular follow-ups with her healthcare professional. Which of the following is the most appropriate supplement to prevent wound failure in this patient?
analysis: In patients with diabetes and those on immunosuppressive therapy (like prednisone and methotrexate), wound healing can be compromised. Vitamin C is known to play a crucial role in collagen synthesis and is important for wound healing. It also has antioxidant properties that can help in reducing oxidative stress, which is beneficial for patients undergoing surgery. Therefore, among the options provided, Vitamin C is the most appropriate supplement to prevent wound failure in this patient.
